accepted.match: "frame" defined differently in composition and animation
accepted.reason: Genuine homonym across sub-fields: composition uses frame for the visible boundary selecting part of a scene; animation uses frame for a single still image in a moving-image sequence. Both definitions are correct in their owning lessons.

Compatible definitions at different depths: representation defines stereotyping as the general mechanism (a generalized belief applied to every member of a group); race-and-media and gender-and-media define the recurring simplified character type as it operates across media texts on specific axes. Same concept, different levels of application; the lessons cross-reference each other.

accepted.match: "omission" defined differently in representation and media-literacy
accepted.reason: Compatible domain-specific uses: representation defines omission as Tuchman's first aspect of symbolic annihilation (a group simply not appearing); media-literacy defines omission as what any message leaves out. Both concern absence but at different levels (pattern across texts vs single message); no contradiction.

accepted.match: "fear appeal" defined differently in advertising and propaganda
accepted.reason: Compatible domain-specific uses: advertising defines the fear appeal as a persuasion technique warning of risk with the product as protection; propaganda defines it as threat-emphasis pushing a prescribed action. Same device, different domains and purposes; both correctly framed in their owning lessons.

The shared text is the four canonical SPJ Code of Ethics principle names (Seek Truth and Report It; Minimize Harm; Act Independently; Be Accountable and Transparent) enumerated in both lessons by design: news-media cites them as journalism's professional norms, media-criticism as the ethics frame for critics. A canonical standards-body list legitimately cited by both; no duplicated prose beyond the principle names.
